56.subject: Botany
56.text: Which one feature is common to leech, cockroach and scorpion?
56.sol: The ventral nerve cord, as its name suggests, is a cord of nervous tissue that runs the length of the animal in the lower part of its body. It is the characteristic of lower chordates like leech, cockroach and scorpion.

133.subject: Botany
133.text: Assertion : Neurospora is commonly called water mould. Reason : It belongs to basidomycetes fungi.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
133.sol: Neurospora is commonly called pink/red bread mould or pink mould. It belongs to class ascomycetes fungi or sac fungi. It is used in experimental genetics as it can be grown easily in a definite medium in laboratory. It is a haploid fungus. It is a heterothallic fungus having + ve and - ve mycelia and somatic fusion of two halpoid nuclei produce a diploid zygote. The zygote by one meiotic and another mitotic divisions forms 8-nuclei and hence ascospores, a characteristic structure of ascomycetes are produced.

297.subject: Botany
297.text: One hormone hastens maturity period in juvenile conifers, a second hormone controls xylem differentiation, while the third hormone increases the tolerance of plants to various stresses. They are respectively
297.sol: Spraying juvenile conifers with gibberellins hastens their maturity period, thus leading to early seed production. Auxin controls xylem differentiation. Abscisic acid (ABA) increases the tolerance of plants to various kinds of stresses therefore, is also known as stress hormone.

1921.subject: Zoology
1921.text: When kidney of a person is damaged, he/she invariably suffers from anaemia because
options: iron and vitamin B ₁₂ are not able to bind to haemoglobin.
1921.sol: Erythropoietin is a glycoprotein produced by the kidney, which regulates red blood cell formation in the bone marrow. During kidney damage, enough erythropoietin required for adequate RBCs production is not synthesised resulting in anaemia.

2027.subject: Zoology
2027.text: Assertion : Small intestine is the principal organ for absorption of nutrients. Reason : Absorption of water, simple sugars and alcohol etc. takes place in small intestine.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
2027.sol: Absorption of substances takes place in different parts of the alimentary canal, like mouth, stomach, small intestine and large intestine. However, maximum absorption occurs in the small intestine. Hence, small intestine is the principal organ for absorption of nutrients. The digestion is completed here and the final products of digestion such as glucose, fructose, fatty acids, glycerol and amino acids are absorbed through the mucosa into the blood stream and lymph. 2143.sol: During transcription, one of the two DNA strands functions as template strand and the other functions as coding strand. Template strand serves as template for transcription whereas coding strand does not take part in transcription. Hence, the m RNA produced has base sequence complementary to template strand while similar to coding strand except that thymine ( T ) is replaced by uracil (U). Here, Coding strand 5^ GTTCGAGTC 3^ Template strand 5^ CAAGCTCAG 3^ Transcript 5^ GUUCGAGUC 3^

46113.text: You are given resistance wire of length 50 cm and a battery of negligible resistance. In which of the following cases is largest amount of heat generated?

When the wire is divided into two parts and both the parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When the wire is divided into four parts and all the four parts are connected to the battery in parallel.
When only half of the wire is connected to the battery.
46113.sol: Let R be the resistance of the wire (a) H₁= V^2 t R (b) Resistance of each part will be R / 2. When they are connected in parallel, the resistance will be R / 4 . Hence, H₂= 4 v^2 t R (c) In case of four wires connected in parallel, the resistance will be R / 8 H₃= 8 V^2 t R (d) H₄= V^2 t [R / 2] = 2 V^2 t R Hence, largest amount of heat will be generated in case of four parts connected in parallel.

58853.subject: Chemistry
58853.text: Which of the following dopant is used in silicon to produce p-type semiconductor?
58853.sol: A p-type semiconductor is created by doping silicon with a trivalent impurity from Group 13. These elements possess three valence electrons, one fewer than silicon. When incorporated into the crystal lattice, they create a hole that acts as a positive charge carrier. Gallium (Ga) is a Group 13 element and serves as a trivalent dopant. Antimony (Sb), arsenic (As), and phosphorus (P) belong to Group 15. These are pentavalent impurities that produce n-type semiconductors by donating an extra electron.

71233.subject: Biology
71233.text: Given below are two statements regarding nitrogen fixation in plants. Statement I - Nitrogen fixing bacteria use high energy to fix each molecule of nitrogen to form ammonia, which is an exothermic reaction. Statement II - Chemoautotrophic bacteria obtain energy during nitrification of ammonia into nitrate, which is an endothermic reaction. In the light of the above statements, select the correct option given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
71233.sol: Statement I is incorrect because biological nitrogen fixation requires a very high input of energy ( 8 ATP for each NH ₃ produced). Since it requires energy, it is an endothermic process, not an exothermic one. Statement II is incorrect because nitrification involves the oxidation of ammonia into nitrite and then into nitrate. Oxidation reactions release energy, making nitrification an exothermic process, not an endothermic one. Chemoautotrophic bacteria utilize this released energy to synthesize their food. Theref

71364.subject: Biology
71364.text: Deficiency of clotting factor VIII or IX in the blood causes _________.
71364.sol: Haemophilia is a genetic disorder that impairs the body's ability to make blood clots, a process needed to stop bleeding. This results in people bleeding for a longer time after an injury, easy bruising, and an increased risk of bleeding inside joints or the brain. Haemophilia A is the most common type and is caused by a deficiency of clotting factor VIII. Haemophilia B is caused by a deficiency of clotting factor IX. Therefore, the deficiency of clotting factor VIII or IX in the blood causes haemophilia. Answer: h

72430.sol: The efficiency of a Carnot engine is given by the formula: = 1 - T_C T_H where T_C is the temperature of the cold reservoir and T_H is the temperature of the hot reservoir. 74435.text: Colour vision in human eyes is the function of photoreceptor cells named
74435.sol: Cone cells, or cones, are photoreceptor cells in the retinas of vertebrate eyes (e.g. the human eye). 75465.sol: - Nimbus clouds are those which bring precipitation, and they usually appear in the sky as dark gray. Nimbus clouds can also bring rain, snow, or hail. - The different types of clouds are cumulus, cirrus, stratus and nimbus.

75921.subject: General Ability
75921.text: Rain shadow effect is associated with
75921.sol: The condition exists because warm moist air rises by orographic lifting to the top of a mountain range. As atmospheric pressure decreases with increasing altitude, the air has expanded and adiabatically cooled to the point that the air reaches its adiabatic dew point. At the adiabatic dew point, moisture condenses onto the mountain and it precipitates on the top and windward sides of the mountain.

Based on number of amino and carboxyl groups, there are acidic (e.g., glutamic acid), basic (lysine) and neutral (valine) amino acids. Similarly, there are aromatic amino acids (tyrosine, phenylalanine, tryptophan). A particular property of amino acids is the ionizable nature of –NH2 and –COOH groups. Hence in solutions of different pH, the structure of amino acids changes.

95197.subject: Botany
95197.text: Which one of the following statements pertaining to plant structure is correct?
options: Cork lacks stomata, but lenticels carry out transpiration.
Passage cells help in transfer of food from cortex to phloem.
Sieve tube possess cytoplasm and nuclei.
Shoot apical meristem has a vascular tissue.
95197.sol: Cork is dead tissue that lacks stomata but lenticels present carries transpiration (0.1-1% only) also carries gaseous exchange. Passage cells are present in endodermis which regulates the unidirectional flow of water and minerals in roots. Sieve tube lacks nuclei and the nucleus of the companion cells regulates its functioning. Shoot apex consists of meristematic tissue only.

95439.subject: Botany
95439.text: With respect to their classification, find the odd one out from the following.
95439.sol: Echinus (sea urchin), Antedon (sea lily), Cucumaria (sea cucumber) belong to phylum Echinodermata. They are all marine with radial symmetry and have an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles. Aplysia (sea hare) is a mollusc.

95595.subject: Botany
95595.text: The unique characteristic of phylum Annelida is
95595.sol: The unique characteristic of phylum Annelida is the presence of nephridia. Nephridia are organs which osmoregulation and excretion. Hermaphrodites are animals in which the male, as well as female reproductive organ, is present in the same organism. This feature is seen in members of Phylum Annelida like an earthworm, but it is also seen in members of other phyla, like that of Phylum Echinodermata. Thus, it is not a feature which is unique to Phylum Annelida.

95681.subject: Botany
95681.text: Which of the following is not the correct match with respect to fungi?
options: Class Common name Mycelium Member Phycomycetes Aquatic fungi Aseptate Mucor/Albugo
Class Common name Mycelium Member Ascomycetes Sac fungi Aseptate Morels, truffles, Aspergillus , Neurospora
Class Common name Mycelium Member Basidiomycetes Club fungi Septate Rust fungi, smut fungi, Agaricus
Class Common name Mycelium Member Deuteromycetes Imperfect fungi Septate Trichoderma , red rot, early blight
95681.sol: Commonly known as sac-fungi, the ascomycetes are mostly multicellular, e.g., Penicillium , or rarely unicellular, e.g., yeast ( Saccharomyces ). They are saprophytic, decomposers, parasitic or coprophilous (growing on dung). Mycelium is branched, septate and non-coenocytic in nature. Some examples are Aspergillus , Claviceps , Neurospora , morels, truffles and Claviceps . Neurospora is used extensively in biochemical and genetic studies.

96071.subject: Botany
96071.text: Which of the following is called the fret membrane?
96071.sol: This membrane is found in the chloroplast. This organelle is present within plants and algae to carry out photosynthesis. They have a double-layered membrane that encloses a matrix called the stroma. In the stroma, a membrane-bound structure is present i.e .thylakoid which arranges as a stack to form granum. Grana connects to each other through stroma lamellae. It is also known as intergranal lamellae or fret lamellae. Space which is present in stroma lamellae is called fret channels and they have enzymes for carbo

96249.subject: Botany
96249.text: A typical process of cell division in a human cell approximately lasts for
96249.sol: In a human eukaryotic cell the whole cell cycle process takes place in about 24 hours. The interphase consumes around 23 hours of the total duration of the cycle. The whole cell division stage is quite fast and short lasting about one hour only.

96395.subject: Botany
96395.text: Which of the following factors play a role in primary productivity?
96395.sol: The primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate at which biomass or organic matter is produced per unit area per unit time by plants (primary producers). Primary productivity depends upon plant species of the area, their photosynthetic capacity, availability of nutrients, solar radiations, precipitation, soil type and a number of other environmental factors.

96420.subject: Botany
options: The ecosystems that are created and maintained by man.
The ecosystem made by the addition of energy and planned manipulation with a natural balance.
Corp lands, orchards, gardens, aquariums, greenhouses etc., are examples for artificial ecosystems.
96420.sol: An ecosystem is a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment. Ecosystem varies greatly in size from a small pond to a large forest or a sea. Forest, grassland and desert are some examples of terrestrial ecosystems; pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are some examples of aquatic ecosystems. Crop fields and an aquarium may also be considered as man-made ecosystems or artificial ecosystems. These are the ecosystems that are maintai

96572.subject: Botany
96572.text: ________ are important decomposers that cause decay and decomposition of dead bodies of plants and animals.
96572.sol: The organic content of the dead and decaying organisms is broken down to inorganic substances by the process called decomposition. It is brought about by decomposers. Decomposition is mainly an oxygen dependent process and its rate is dependent on chemical composition and climatic factors. Decomposers play a vital role in energy flow through the ecosystem and also in making available the essential nutrients to the producers. Saprophytes are organisms that show saprophytic nutrition where the organisms digest decayi

96650.subject: Botany
96650.text: Of the following _________ represents the largest man made ecosystem.
96650.sol: Man-made ecosystems are a copy of natural ecosystems created by man. The conditions of natural ecosystems are replicated in the man-made ecosystem. These are sustained by human interventions. Examples include aquarium, zoo, botanical gardens, park, agriculture land. Out of these, the agriculture field represents the largest man-made ecosystem.

96691.subject: Botany
96691.text: In root nodules of leguminous plants, the function of leg-hemoglobin during biological nitrogen fixation is
96691.sol: Leghemoglobin is an oxygen-carrying protein, somewhat similar to the hemoglobin of blood, that helps maintain the low oxygen tension necessary for effective nitrogen fixation. This is an essential component for nitrogen fixation by legumes. Leghemoglobin is produced as a result of symbiotic association between bacteroid and plant. The major role of leghemoglobin involves protection of nitrogenase enzyme from denaturation, if exposed to atmospheric concentration of oxygen, but at the same time supply of ample amount

96693.subject: Botany
96693.text: How many of the following plants have an association with Rhizobium ? [Sweet pea, Lentils, Garden pea, Alfalfa, Alnus , Frankia , Soybean, Clover beans]
96693.sol: Alnus and Frankia are not associated with the legume family, rest all are legume plants. Legume plants show symbiotic association with Rhizobium . Rhizobium is a bacterial genus associated with the formation of root nodules in plants of the legume family. These are symbiotic bacteria which take in nitrogen from the atmosphere and pass it on to the plant, allowing it to grow in soil low in nitrogen.

96972.subject: Botany
96972.text: The ovary is half inferior in the flowers of
96972.sol: In perigynous flower, all the floral whorls are occured at the same level of height on the thalamus so they are called half superior or half inferior. E.g.: Rose, peach & Prunus. The ovary is half - inferior in flowers of peach.

97203.subject: Botany
97203.text: Read the given statements about auxins and state whether they are true or false: a. Auxin promotes apical dominance. b. Auxins have a negative impact on cytokinin levels. c. F.W. Went isolated auxins from the coleoptiles of the oat plant. d. Auxin promotes flowering in the pineapple plants.
97203.sol: F.W. Went isolated the auxins from the Avena coleoptiles . Auxins promote apical dominance by inhibiting the growth of lateral buds. Auxins promote flowering in plants like pineapple as it is a growth-promoting hormone-like cytokinin. Auxins do not affect the cytokinin level negatively as they are not antagonistic in function.

97539.subject: Botany
options: pyriform and bear 2 flagella (one longitudinal and another transverse)
pear-shaped and bear 2 flagella that are laterally attached
pyriform and bear 2-8, equal and apical flagella
pear-shaped and bear 2-8, equal and apical flagella
97539.sol: Phaeophyceae or the brown algae inhabit the marine environment. These organisms show sexual as well as asexual means of reproduction wherein the sexual reproduction may be monogamous, isogamous, or anisogamous whereas the asexual reproduction takes place with the help of bi-flagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal flagella laterally attached to it.

305646.subject: Physics
305646.text: A steel metre scale measures the correct length at 16^ C . Evaluate the percentage error if this scale is employed on a winter day when the temperature is 6^ C . The coefficient of linear expansion of steel is given as 11 10⁻⁶ ^ C⁻¹ .
305646.sol: The true length of an object is L . The scale is calibrated at T₁ = 16^ C . At T₂ = 6^ C , the change in temperature is T = 6^ C - 16^ C = -10^ C . Due to thermal contraction, the length of one division on the scale becomes d' = d(1 + T) . The measured length L_m is given by L_m = L 1 + T L(1 - T) . The error in measurement is L = L_m - L = -L T . Percentage error = L L 100 = - T 100 . Substituting the given values: Percentage error = -(11 10⁻⁶) (-10) 100 = 11 10⁻³ = 0.011 % .

305036.subject: Physics
305036.chapter: Bohr's Model and Physics of the Atom
305036.text: Determine the energy of a hydrogen atom in the first excited state if the potential energy is taken to be zero in the ground state.
305036.sol: The total energy of an electron in the n^ th orbit of a hydrogen atom is given by E_n = - 13.6 n^2 eV . The potential energy is twice the total energy, so U_n = 2E_n = - 27.2 n^2 eV . In the ground state ( n=1 ), the standard potential energy is U₁ = -27.2 eV . If the potential energy in the ground state is taken to be zero, the reference level of potential energy is shifted by +27.2 eV . Since kinetic energy remains unaffected by the choice of reference, the total energy of every state also increases by +27.2 eV .

Energy released per fission is E₁ = 200 MeV = 200 10^6 1.6 10⁻¹⁹ J = 3.2 10⁻¹¹ J . Total energy released is E = N E₁ = 1.794 10¹⁹ 3.2 10⁻¹¹ J 5.7 10^8 J .

306633.text: A radioactive sample has a decay constant . The half-life and average-life of the sample are respectively
306633.sol: The radioactive decay law is given by N = N₀ e^ - t For half-life T_ 1/2 , the number of active nuclei becomes half of its initial value, so N = N₀ 2 N₀ 2 = N₀ e^ - T_ 1/2 e^ T_ 1/2 = 2 T_ 1/2 = 2 The average life or mean life T_ avg is defined as the sum of the lifetimes of all individual nuclei divided by the total number of nuclei, which is the reciprocal of the decay constant. T_ avg = 1 Thus, the half-life and average-life are 2 and 1 respectively.

6a7a1ff854f34e55ae32550b.sol: The horizontal distance covered in time t = 2 s is x = 20 3 m. The horizontal component of initial velocity is: u_x = x t = 20 3 2 = 10 3 m/s The vertical component of initial velocity is related to the horizontal component by the angle of projection = 60^ : u_y = u_x 60^ = 10 3 3 = 30 m/s The height H at which the particle strikes the wall is the vertical displacement at t = 2 s: H = u_y t - 1 2 gt^2 H = 30(2) - 1 2 (10)(2)^2 H = 60 - 20 = 40 m Answer: 40 m

6a7a1ff8e2ba6d14402d5668.text: A sample of sodium bicarbonate ( NaHCO₃ ) is heated strongly until a constant weight is achieved. If the total mass loss due to the evolution of gases is 3.1 g, what was the initial mass of the sample? (Given: Molar mass of Na, H, C and O are 23 , 1 , 12 and 16 g mol ⁻¹ respectively)
6a7a1ff8e2ba6d14402d5668.sol: The thermal decomposition of sodium bicarbonate is given by: 2NaHCO₃(s) Na₂CO₃(s) + H₂O(g) + CO₂(g) Molar mass of NaHCO₃ = 23 + 1 + 12 + 3 16 = 84 g mol ⁻¹ From the balanced equation, heating 2 moles of NaHCO₃ ( 2 84 = 168 g) results in the loss of 1 mole of H₂O and 1 mole of CO₂ as gases. Total mass loss for 2 moles of NaHCO₃ = 18 g ( H₂O ) + 44 g ( CO₂ ) = 62 g. Let the initial mass of the sample be m . Since 62 g of mass is lost from 168 g of NaHCO₃ , a mass loss of 3.1 g corresponds to: m = 168 62 3.1 = 8.4 g.
